🛡️ FREESTONE COUNTY ARES OPERATOR LEVELS EXPLAINED STANDARDS
Level 1 - Operator BASIC PRIVILEGES

New person with no prior experience. Can set up in a building/facility and assist an experienced operator.

Level 2 - Field Operator / Spotter FIELD & SPOTTER

Certified to operate in the field independently and deploy as a mobile storm spotter during SKYWARN weather activations.

Level 3 - Net Control Station (NCS) NCS PRIVILEGES

Can do all of Level 1 & 2 + access to all NCS features like official Net Script (ARRL preamble) and live NetLogger check-ins.

Level 4 - Assistant EC (AEC) ALERT DISPATCH

Assists the EC in all aspects. Granted all operator permissions plus emergency page-out, siren activation, and deployment controls.

Level 5 - County EMC ALL EXCEPT ALERTS

County Emergency Management Coordinator. Has ALL app permissions EXCEPT alert features (no ham radio page-out dispatch).

Level 6 - Emergency Coordinator (EC) ROOT MASTER EC

Brian Davis (KG5TZT). Master authority with ALL app permissions (EC security desk authorizations, paging, alerts, and bypass).

OFFICIAL FREESTONE CO. ARES NET CONTROL SCRIPT
1. OPENING & NETLOGGER ANNOUNCEMENT TRANSMIT

"Good evening. This is ( call sign ) ( name ) ( location ). I will be your net control station this evening for the Freestone County Amateur Radio Emergency Services Net. You do not need to be a resident of Freestone County or a member of ARES to check-in. If you would like to follow along with check ins go to Netlogger and search up Freestone County ARES."

⚡ (let repeater drop)
2. FREQUENCIES & BACKUP REPEATERS TRANSMIT

"This net is held each Sunday evening at 8:00pm on 145.110 - offset and a Tone of 146.2 known as the Fairfield repeater.
NOTE: if this repeater is not available the net will meet on: 146.760 – offset and a Tone of 136.5 known as the Wortham DFY Repeater.
Freestone County ARES Primary Simplex Frequency is 146.580 with a tone of 123."

⚡ (let repeater drop)
3. FORMAL TRAFFIC CALLS

"At this time we will take any EMERGENCY or Priority traffic."

(handle traffic or acknowledge nothing heard)

"We will now take any Health and Welfare traffic."

(handle traffic or acknowledge nothing heard)

"We will now take Routine traffic."

(handle traffic or acknowledge nothing heard)
4. DIRECTED STATION CHECK-INS
A. MOBILE STATIONS:

"At this time we will take any mobile station that would like to check in, please come now with your call sign, name and current location."

(take check ins)
B. LIAISON STATIONS:

"Are there any liaison stations that would like to check in this evening? A liaison station is one that is affiliated with another emergency service or served agency such as the American Red Cross."

(take liaison stations)
C. ECHOLINK STATIONS:

"Echolink: any stations wishing to check in on echolink please call now with your call sign, name, and location."

(take checkins)
D. GENERAL CHECK-INS:

"We will now take general check ins. I would like to remind everyone that this is a directed net and for stations to come one at a time with their callsign, name and current location."

(take check ins)
5. QUESTIONS, COMMENTS & TRAINING

"Are there any questions or comments for the net this evening? (if you would like you may insert a training topic here)"

(handle questions)
6. NET CLOSING & REPEATER RETURN

"I would like to thank everyone for checking in this evening.
This is (callsign) now closing the Freestone County Amateur Radio Emergency Services Net at (Local Time), and returning the repeater back to its normal amateur use."

⚠️ (don’t forget to sign out with your callsign after your last transmission)

PACE TRANSITION DECISION MATRIX STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
COMMAND RULE: NIMS / COML COMPLIANT
LEVEL 1: PRIMARY OUTAGE

If NCS fails to reach FF 110 after 3 calls, or severe repeater desense occurs:

DIRECTIVE: "All stations QSY to Alternate WRTM 760 (146.760 -0.600 T136.5)"
LEVEL 2: ALTERNATE OUTAGE

If WRTM 760 is also dead or power grid fails countywide:

DIRECTIVE: "All stations QSY to Contingency ARES TAC (146.580 Simplex T123.0)"
LEVEL 3: SIMPLEX RELAYS

If handheld HTs cannot penetrate county distances:

DIRECTIVE: Simplex relays are handled by member base stations and vehicle mobile radios to bridge field operators.
LEVEL 4: EMERGENCY DISPATCH

Total RF blackout, EMP, or localized communication loss:

DIRECTIVE: Keep trying simplex frequencies, use GMRS CH 6-8, and deploy physical couriers with written ICS-213s.

FREESTONE COUNTY ARES NET CONTROL SCRIPT

STANDARDIZED ARRL / COUNTY ARES OPERATING PREAMBLE
1. OPENING PREAMBLE (20:00 LOCAL / 01:00Z) READ CLEARLY & DELIBERATELY

"Calling all stations, calling all stations. This is [YOUR CALLSIGN], my name is [YOUR NAME], acting as Net Control Station for the Freestone County Amateur Radio Emergency Service (ARES) weekly training net. This net meets every Sunday at 2000 hours local time on the W5NFL Fairfield repeater, 145.110 MHz, minus offset, with a tone of 146.2 Hz, with backup on the WRTM 760 repeater, 146.760 MHz, tone 136.5 Hz."

"The purpose of this net is to practice emergency message handling, test equipment, exchange training information, and maintain readiness to support Freestone County Emergency Management, local first responders, and served agencies in times of communication failure."

🚨 2. EMERGENCY OR PRIORITY TRAFFIC BREAK

"Is there any emergency, priority, or time-sensitive traffic for the net? Any station with emergency traffic, call Net Control now."

[Pause 5 seconds. If traffic is heard, suspend net operations and handle immediately.]

3. ORDERLY ROLL CALL & CHECK-IN SEQUENCE

A. Mobile, Portable, and Short-Time Stations: "We will now take check-ins from mobile, portable, or stations with limited time. Please call Net Control with your callsign phonetically, your name, and your location."

B. Appointed Officers & Liaisons: "I will now call for check-ins from our Emergency Coordinator Brian Davis (KG5TZT), Assistant ECs, and County Emergency Management officials."

C. General County ARES Members: "We will now begin general check-ins for Freestone County ARES operators. Please check in with your callsign, name, whether you are on commercial or backup power, and if you have any announcements."

D. Out-of-County & Visitors: "We welcome all visitors and neighboring county stations. Please call Net Control now."

4. ANNOUNCEMENTS, TRAINING TOPIC & WINLINK DRILL

"We will now take announcements from Emergency Coordinator Brian Davis (KG5TZT), followed by tonight's 5-minute training topic and confirmation of digital Winlink check-ins on Ch 28 (144.975 MHz)."

5. CLOSING PREAMBLE & REPEATER RETURN

"Are there any late check-ins, comments, or corrections for the net before we close? [Pause]. Seeing none, we thank the W5NFL repeater trustee for the use of this repeater, and we thank all stations who checked in tonight. We had 15 check-ins. The net is now closed at 20:45 local time and the repeater is returned to normal amateur service. 73 to all, this is [CALLSIGN] clear."

10-SECOND ON-AIR SPOTTER REPORT

READ CLEARLY OVER FF 110 OR WRTM 760

Keep voice transmission under 10 seconds. Do not tie up repeater during severe weather nets. Read the following formatted report:

TRANSMISSION READ-OUT:

"Net Control, this is Storm Spotter KG5TZT with a SEVERE REPORT. Location: US-84 West at FM 488, 3 miles West of Fairfield, Grid EM11xq. Time: 18:22 Local. Phenomenon: Rotating wall cloud with 1.25 inch hail and estimated 65 MPH wind. Trees down on Hwy 84. Moving East at 35 MPH. Over."

NWS REPORTING CHECKLIST:
  • 1. Who: Your Callsign & Spotter ID
  • 2. What: Specific severe phenomenon (Hail size, Wind speed, Rotation)
  • 3. Where: Exact distance & direction from city center / cross streets
  • 4. When: Exact time phenomenon occurred (not when reported)
📖

NWS FORT WORTH SPOTTER CRITERIA

OFFICIAL FREESTONE COUNTY ARES PROTOCOL
CRITERIA TO REPORT IMMEDIATELY:
🌪️ TORNADOES & ROTATION Tornado on the ground, persistent rotating wall cloud (>= 5 min), or funnel cloud lowering.
🧊 HAIL ≥ 1.00" (QUARTER) Quarter size (1.00") or larger. Pea/dime/nickel are non-severe and should NOT be reported.
💨 DAMAGING WIND ≥ 58 MPH Measured or estimated gusts causing trees down, large limbs snapped, or roof damage.
🌊 FLASH FLOODING Water rising rapidly over roadways, impassable bridges, or overflowing creeks.
